The purpose of the cooling system is to ensure that the engine stays within the optimum operating temperature.
The cooling system removes excess heat from the engine and ensures that the engine gets up to the correct temperature as soon as possible after starting.
A cooling system is also required to prevent the internal engine parts from melting from the heat of the burning fuel.
(Página 241 del manual 'Learning to drive')

VISIBILITY  
   
8 Rear-view  
8.1 Obligatory requirements regarding rear-view mirrors
The following are obligatory requirements for vehicles within categories M1 and N1:
A rear-view interior mirror. This must comply with the field of vision in accordance with the regulations. Should the rear-view interior mirror not accord the required vision through it, that allows viewing of the roadway, when on flat ground of the horizon to a distance of 60 metres behind the vehicle and a width of 20 metres then the rear view mirrors becomes optional but the vehicle must have a second exterior, side mirror, on the right hand side that is the nearside (the side closest to the pavement.
An exterior mirror fitted on the left hand side (that is the offside of the vehicle) allowing the minimum vision of the horizon to a distance of 10 metres behind it and a width of 2.50 metres.
An exterior mirror on the right hand side (nearside, closest to the pavement) remains optional, unless fitted for the reasons as stated above. When fitted it must give a field of vision as prescribed within the regulations.
(Página 90 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Seat belts
 
7.4 The correct fastening of seat belts
The seat belt must be properly secured (buckled-up) and adjusted correctly so that it is neither too loose nor too tight for comfortable travel.
If the seat belt is slack the body travels a greater distance during an impact and is more likely to be hit against the steering wheel or windshield.
If seatbelts are not snugly fastened, the seatbelt loses effectiveness and can lead to injuries in accidents.
The use of seat belt locking clips or tension adjusters is prohibited and dangerous, because it reduces the effectiveness of the seat belt.
(Página 77 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
9 The negative effects of speed
 
Through the driver’s vision, 90% of the information needed for good driving is received: the condition and configuration of the road, signalling, distances, speeds etc. Hence, the importance of having the largest possible zone of vision when driving. Speed, among other factors, causes a decrease in the useful field of vision, which results in a tunnel vision effect. Therefore, as speed increases the driver’s field of vision is reduced eventually resulting in only objects in the centre of the roadway being clearly visible. The peripheral vision is steadily reduced as speed increases also.
 
(Página 178 del manual 'Learning to drive')
